cards.explanation: The answer is the earth, friends. Ezekiel says, "…the earth shone with His glory." Think about that. Not a spotlight on one building, the whole earth lit up.

The answer is that Ezekiel falls facedown, friends. He says, "I fell facedown…" He's seen this kind of vision before, by the River Kebar and when He came to destroy the city, and he still goes straight to the ground. Facedown is how he meets the glory.

The answer is True, friends. Ezekiel says, "…the glory of the LORD entered the temple through the gate facing east." He's facedown on the ground while it happens. The glory comes in by the very gate where the man brought him back to.

The answer is the Spirit, friends. Ezekiel says, "…the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court…" Facedown one moment, lifted and brought into the inner court the next. The Spirit is the one who does it.

The answer is that He will dwell among the Israelites forever, friends. He says, "…where I will dwell among the Israelites forever." The throne, the soles of His feet, and then the promise to stay. That word "forever" is the big one.

The answer is False, friends. Nothing got overlooked. The voice says, "…they defiled My holy name by the abominations they committed. Therefore I have consumed them in My anger." It's a heavy part of the passage, and He says it plainly.

The answer is ashamed, friends. He says, "…describe the temple to the people of Israel, so that they may be ashamed of their iniquities." Then He adds, "Let them measure the plan…" In verse 11 He says, "…if they are ashamed of all they have done, then make known to them the design of the temple…"

The answer is True, friends. The voice says, "…if they are ashamed of all they have done, then make known to them the design of the temple…" Then He adds, "Write it down in their sight…" The people get to see it in writing, so they can keep the whole design and carry it out.

The answer is that it will be most holy, friends. The voice says, "All its surrounding territory on top of the mountain will be most holy." Then He says, "Yes, this is the law of the temple." The law covers all the temple's surrounding territory, not just the building.

The answer is that He will accept the people, friends. The Lord GOD says, "Then I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD." It comes after the seven days of atonement for the altar, when the priests present the burnt offerings and peace offerings. It's a good place to end the chapter.
